name: Department of Health and Human Services
type: Cabinet Department (parent of CMS, NIH, FDA, CDC, IHS, ONC, ARPA-H)
description: HHS just realigned. As of January 2026, OMAS (the Office of Mission Acquisition Solutions) is the new contracting activity for all common IT, professional services, and what used to flow through ACF and AHRQ. The department dropped from 13 contracting activities to 10. If you sell common IT or advisory services into HHS, your contracting officer moved. If you sell mission-unique work to NIH, CDC, CMS, FDA, HRSA, IHS, ASPR, ARPA-H, or OIG, you stay where you are.
mmtRead: HHS is two stories now, not one. The mission-unique side (NIH for research IT, CMS for claims, FDA for surveillance, ARPA-H for OTA-funded R&D) still buys at the operating division. The common side (laptops, cloud, cybersecurity tools, advisory services, training) flows through OMAS strategic buying centers under EO 14240 and OMB M-25-31. Your BD calendar needs both maps: the operating-division map for mission, the OMAS SBC map for common. Expect the picture to keep moving. The FY2026 Budget in Brief proposed consolidating 28 operating divisions to 15 and closing 5 regional offices; Congress's FY2026 Labor-HHS bill did not fold HRSA into an Administration for a Healthy America, and the FY2027 request (April 2026) proposes the 28-to-15 consolidation again. FY2027 opened October 1, 2026 under a continuing resolution to December 11, 2026 that bars new starts.

The NITAAC GWACs take their last new orders October 29, 2026, so the HHS-wide IT paths after that date are GSA's. FY2027 opened under a continuing resolution to December 11, 2026.

items.why_it_matters: eCR closes the loop between EHRs and public health surveillance. The 2026 milestone is 42 of 59 ELC-funded health departments processing electronic case reports into production (PHDS 2026 milestones document, cited in MMT's September 11, 2026 issue). The expansion support contract reported awarded September 11, 2026 to J Michael Consulting with Deloitte is the delivery side. Vendor surface includes EHR-side connector work, jurisdictional ingestion, and case routing.

Modernizes how mortality data flows between vital records, CDC, and downstream public health users. The 2026 milestone is FHIR-based mortality data exchange in 23 jurisdictions. FHIR-mediated APIs and provenance tracking are core.

NBS is the NEDSS Base System, the case management application jurisdictions run for notifiable disease surveillance; MMT's tracker carries its modernization as awarded to Enquizit (about $48.2M). The replatform creates an integration surface for jurisdictional case management and reporting tools.
1CDP framing consolidates the CDC data platform. Capture moves are around shared services, identity, and reusable analytics.
Governance posture shapes how data-sharing agreements, technical standards, and partner onboarding work. Leading indicator for tooling and policy-implementation services.

policyModule.title: Data Modernization Action Plan (DMAP)
confirmed_facts: DMAP is FDA's data modernization framework anchored on three components: data drivers (high-value driver projects), repeatable data practices, and people/external partnerships.
DMAP positions data modernization as a regulatory mission enabler, supporting FDA's product-area centers, review activities, and post-market surveillance.
The published DMAP is a high-level strategy document; current FDA implementation status is communicated through individual center activity and follow-on publications.
vendor_watch: Repeatable data practices: shared services, common data models, reusable pipelines across centers.
Talent and external partnerships: workforce enablement, academic collaboration, public-private partnership posture.
Regulatory mission alignment: tooling that supports review, post-market surveillance, and inspection workflows.
Currentness caveat: DMAP framing should be paired with newer FDA implementation sources before publishing capture briefs to clients.

name: Health Resources and Services Administration
type: HHS Operating Division (health workforce, health centers, HIV/AIDS, maternal and child health, organ transplantation)
description: Funds and oversees the Health Center Program, the Ryan White HIV/AIDS Program, the National Health Service Corps and other workforce programs, the Maternal and Child Health Block Grant, the 340B Drug Pricing Program and the Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network. A grant-maker first; its contracting sits behind those programs in data systems, program support and the OPTN Modernization Initiative.
mmtRead: HRSA buys less IT than CMS or VA, and what it buys sits behind grant programs: reporting systems, data platforms and program support. The OPTN Modernization Initiative is the one live multi-vendor contracting story, with a December 2025 award to UNOS for OPTN operations including the national matching system and a task order to CVP for policy process and committee support. The 2025 proposal to fold HRSA into an Administration for a Healthy America did not get through Congress's FY2026 Labor-HHS bill, which kept HRSA funded as its own agency; the FY2027 request proposes the merger again.

policyModule.title: HHS reorganization and HRSA
confirmed_facts: HHS announced on March 27, 2025 a reorganization creating an Administration for a Healthy America from HRSA, SAMHSA, OASH, ATSDR and NIOSH.

A federal court granted a preliminary injunction against parts of the reorganization and layoffs (New York v. Kennedy), finding the Executive Branch lacks authority to make wholesale changes to agencies Congress created.
Congress's bipartisan FY2026 Labor-HHS bill rejected the large-scale restructuring and preserved HRSA funding; it requires a detailed plan before any CDC functions move.
The FY2027 President's budget again requests HRSA programs inside a proposed Administration for a Healthy America.
policyModule.vendor_implication: Plan against HRSA as it exists: bureaus, program offices and the OPTN Modernization Initiative. Treat the merger as a signal to watch in the FY2027 appropriations cycle, not as an organization to sell into.

contractorRead: HRSA is a grants agency with a narrow contracting lane. The live capture story is the OPTN Modernization Initiative, where a multi-vendor model replaces one contractor and each function (operations, policy support, IT, patient safety) is competed separately. Beyond OPTN, HRSA buys data systems and program support behind its grant programs, usually through HHS-wide and GSA vehicles. Position for OPTN functions not yet awarded, and for reporting and data work tied to health centers, Ryan White and 340B.

name: Administration for Strategic Preparedness and Response (with BARDA)
type: HHS Operating Division for preparedness and response; BARDA is its medical countermeasures development arm
description: Leads HHS preparedness and response: the Strategic National Stockpile, the National Disaster Medical System, hospital preparedness, and BARDA's advanced development of vaccines, therapeutics, diagnostics and devices for CBRN threats, pandemic influenza and emerging infectious diseases. Buys development of products, not enterprise IT.
mmtRead: ASPR is a countermeasures and preparedness funder, not an enterprise IT shop. The doors are BARDA's Broad Agency Announcement on SAM.gov, the DRIVe EZ-BAA for awards under $750,000, and other transactions under 42 U.S.C. 247d-7e. The 2025 HHS reorganization proposed moving ASPR into CDC and BARDA into a new office; Congress funded ASPR at $3.7 billion for FY2026 including $1 billion for BARDA and required a plan before CDC functions move. Health IT vendors reach ASPR through preparedness data and situational awareness needs, and through BARDA's interest in digital health tools for health security.

policyModule.title: ASPR partnering doors and the reorganization question
confirmed_facts: BARDA's Broad Agency Announcement solicits proposals for advanced research and development of medical countermeasures against CBRN threats, pandemic influenza and emerging infectious diseases.
DRIVe runs the EZ-BAA for awards under $750,000 and BAA Special Instructions for larger projects.
BARDA holds other transaction authority under 42 U.S.C. 247d-7e(c)(5).

In March 2025 HHS announced the transfer of ASPR to CDC as part of its reorganization; Congress's FY2026 bill provided $3.7 billion for ASPR including $1 billion for BARDA and requires a plan before CDC functions move (reporting on the bill).
policyModule.vendor_implication: Engage BARDA through the BAA, DRIVe or a TechWatch meeting; engage preparedness offices through readiness requirements. Do not wait on the reorganization to settle before engaging, and do not build a plan that assumes BARDA sits anywhere but ASPR until Congress acts.

contractorRead: ASPR is a development funder. The winning motion is a countermeasure, diagnostic, device or health security tool with a development plan, taken through the BAA or DRIVe, sometimes as an other transaction with cost share. For health IT firms the openings are narrower: preparedness data, situational awareness and health care readiness systems bought by ASPR's response offices, and digital tools BARDA funds through DRIVe. Track the reorganization for where budget lines land, not for whether BARDA keeps buying.
